narrative:

The strongest factor increasing that risk was your third-year class decile. Your value was 1, while accepted students averaged near 5.8; this was the most influential feature and it pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most important factor was your LSAT score. At 37, you were very close to the accepted-student average of about 37.2, and this factor actually pushed toward passing. The third most important factor was your first-year class decile. Your value was 2, compared with an accepted-student average of about 6.0, and this also increased the predicted risk of failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.80 was strong, but it was not among the top drivers of this decision.

To strengthen a future application, focus on the academic signals the model weighted most heavily: seek advising about your law-school performance, consider additional coursework or experiences that demonstrate readiness for rigorous legal study, and retake the LSAT only if you can meaningfully improve it. Also ask admissions for feedback and apply to a balanced range of programs.
